name: aor-batch-exec
display_name: Agent of Record: approved batch executor
description: Runs one existing script a person has read and approved, by relative name under one folder, or saves and runs a complete script text in one step. No command, arguments, environment, working directory, timeout or elevation can be supplied.
long_description:
The approved batch executor from the Agent of Record repository, packaged as an MCP Bundle.

It exposes two tools. `run_batch_file` takes the relative name of a `.bat`/`.cmd` (Windows) or `.sh` (macOS, Linux) file that already exists under `<tooling root>/CommandJobs`. `run_job` takes a plain filename and the complete script text (up to 64 KB), saves it under that same folder, and runs it exactly as `run_batch_file` would. Neither caller can supply a command string, arguments, an interpreter, a working directory, environment variables, an output directory, a timeout override or an elevation option. Absolute, drive-qualified, UNC and environment-variable paths are refused before any process exists, and so is anything that resolves outside the folder after symlinks and junctions are followed.

Every job runs with a fixed 300 second timeout and process-tree kill, 5 MB output caps, one job at a time (a second call while one runs returns EXECUTOR_BUSY and starts nothing), no console, no elevation and no interactive input. Every run writes an operation record under `CommandJobs/Logs/ops` with status ACCEPTED, STARTED, COMPLETED, FAILED or TIMED_OUT, so a lost reply is read back rather than rerun. The reply carries the first 1,000 and last 3,000 characters of stdout and stderr and 25 entries per file list; the complete result is in the result file it names. Deliverables belong under `<tooling root>/Outputs`; the approved script declares its own destination with a `COWORK_OUTPUT` directive that the server verifies.

The unit of approval is a file a person can read in full before it runs. The agent proposes the script, the person approves it, and the executor runs that named file and nothing else.

tools.name: run_batch_file
tools.description: Execute an existing, approved .bat/.cmd (Windows) or .sh (macOS, Linux) file under <tooling root>/CommandJobs, named by relative path. Returns stdout, stderr, exit code, timing and every file touched.

tools.name: run_job
tools.description: Save a complete script text under <tooling root>/CommandJobs by plain filename (replacing a file of that name) and run it exactly as run_batch_file would, with the same limits, logs and operation record.

tooling_root.title: Tooling root
tooling_root.description: The one folder the executor is confined to. Scripts run only from <root>/CommandJobs and deliverables go under <root>/Outputs; both are created if absent. Use your agent-of-record clone to get the shipped jobs, or an empty folder to start clean.

config_root.title: Cowork config root (optional)
config_root.description: Folder holding cowork-memory/cowork-lessons.md if you keep an operating corpus. Leave empty otherwise; the executor then serves no operating-rules reminder.
